import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Ledger.Chi
import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Ledger.DedekindColength

/-!
# The six-term cohomology slice of a short exact sequence of sheaves

For a short exact sequence `0 ⟶ X₁ ⟶ X₂ ⟶ X₃ ⟶ 0` of sheaves of `R`-modules on a small
site, this file packages — **once, and elementwise** — the degree-`≤ 1` slice of the long
exact cohomology sequence

    0 → H⁰X₁ → H⁰X₂ → H⁰X₃ →δ→ H¹X₁ → H¹X₂ → H¹X₃

obtained from mathlib's covariant `Ext`-sequence for the cohomology carrier
`Sheaf.HModule = Ext(constModuleSheaf, ·)`: the connecting map `HModule.delta`, the four
`Function.Exact` facts, injectivity at the left end and surjectivity of `H¹X₁ → H¹X₂`
when `H¹X₃` vanishes.

On top of the slice sit the two consumers of the χ-ledger:

* **finiteness transfer** (`HModule.moduleFinite_middle`, `moduleFinite_left_zero`,
  `moduleFinite_left_succ`): dimension bookkeeping between the terms of the sequence,
  via the division-ring extension lemma `FiniteDimensional.of_exact`;
* **additivity of χ** (`Sheaf.chi_eq_add_of_shortExact`): when `H¹X₃ = 0` and the five
  remaining modules are finite, `χ X₂ = χ X₁ + χ X₃` — the alternating-sum identity
  `AlgebraicGeometry.finrank_alt_sum_eq_zero_of_exact₅` applied to the slice.

The transports from mathlib's `(mk₀ f).postcomp`-spelling to `HModule.map` are definitional
(`Ext`-postcomposition on both sides); each slot of the slice is nevertheless a named
lemma, so downstream files never re-derive the sequence inline.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite

section FiniteDimensional

variable {K V₁ V₂ V₃ : Type*} [DivisionRing K]
  [AddCommGroup V₁] [Module K V₁] [AddCommGroup V₂] [Module K V₂]
  [AddCommGroup V₃] [Module K V₃]

/-- **Extension lemma for finite dimensionality.** If `V₁ → V₂ → V₃` is exact at `V₂` and
the outer terms are finite-dimensional, so is the middle: the kernel of `V₂ → V₃` is the
image of the finite `V₁`, and the coimage embeds into the finite `V₃`. (Mathlib's
`Module.Finite.of_exact` asks for surjectivity of the second map; over a division ring the
corestriction to the range removes that hypothesis.) -/
theorem FiniteDimensional.of_exact (f : V₁ →ₗ[K] V₂) (g : V₂ →ₗ[K] V₃)
    (h : Function.Exact f g) [FiniteDimensional K V₁] [FiniteDimensional K V₃] :
    FiniteDimensional K V₂ := by
  have hexact : Function.Exact f g.rangeRestrict := fun y => by
    rw [← h y]
    exact ⟨fun hy => congrArg Subtype.val hy, fun hy => Subtype.ext hy⟩
  exact Module.Finite.of_exact hexact g.surjective_rangeRestrict
..... decls .....

  vanishes (e.g. skyscrapers, affine schemes).

The dimension counts are only meaningful when the cohomology modules are finite; no
finiteness hypothesis is imposed here (`finrank` silently reads `0` on infinite-dimensional
spaces), and the finiteness bookkeeping is done downstream where it can be discharged.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite

namespace CategoryTheory.Sheaf

variable {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
  {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} R)]

namespace HModule

variable {F G : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)}

/-- **Transport of cohomology along a sheaf isomorphism.** A sheaf isomorphism `e : F ≅ G`
induces an `R`-linear equivalence `Hⁿ(F) ≃ₗ[R] Hⁿ(G)` in every degree, with forward and
inverse maps the functorial `HModule.map` of the two legs of `e`. -/
noncomputable def mapEquiv (e : F ≅ G) (n : ℕ) : HModule F n ≃ₗ[R] HModule G n :=
  { HModule.map e.hom n with
    invFun := HModule.map e.inv n
    left_inv := fun x => by
      change HModule.map e.inv n (HModule.map e.hom n x) = x
      rw [← HModule.map_comp_apply, e.hom_inv_id, HModule.map_id_apply]
    right_inv := fun x => by
      change HModule.map e.hom n (HModule.map e.inv n x) = x
      rw [← HModule.map_comp_apply, e.inv_hom_id, HModule.map_id_apply] }

@[simp]
lemma mapEquiv_apply (e : F ≅ G) {n : ℕ} (x : HModule F n) :
    mapEquiv e n x = HModule.map e.hom n x :=
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma mapEquiv_symm_apply (e : F ≅ G) {n : ℕ} (y : HModule G n) :
    (mapEquiv e n).symm y = HModule.map e.inv n y :=
  rfl

end HModule

/-- `h⁰ F`: the `R`-dimension of the degree-zero cohomology of the sheaf `F` of
`R`-modules (`0` when `H⁰(F)` is not finite-dimensional). -/
noncomputable def h0 (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)) : ℕ :=
  Module.finrank R (HModule F 0)

/-- `h¹ F`: the `R`-dimension of the degree-one cohomology of the sheaf `F` of
`R`-modules (`0` when `H¹(F)` is not finite-dimensional). -/
noncomputable def h1 (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)) : ℕ :=
  Module.finrank R (HModule F 1)

/-- **The (truncated) Euler characteristic** `χ F = h⁰ F − h¹ F`, in `ℤ`. On a curve all
higher cohomology vanishes and this is the honest Euler characteristic; in general it is
the degree-`≤ 1` truncation. -/
noncomputable def chi (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)) : ℤ :=
  (h0 F : ℤ) - (h1 F : ℤ)

variable {F G : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)}

/-- `h⁰` is invariant under sheaf isomorphism. -/
theorem h0_congr (e : F ≅ G) : h0 F = h0 G :=
  (HModule.mapEquiv e 0).finrank_eq

/-- `h¹` is invariant under sheaf isomorphism. -/
theorem h1_congr (e : F ≅ G) : h1 F = h1 G :=
  (HModule.mapEquiv e 1).finrank_eq

/-- `χ` is invariant under sheaf isomorphism. -/
theorem chi_congr (e : F ≅ G) : chi F = chi G := by
  rw [chi, chi, h0_congr e, h1_congr e]

/-- `h¹ F = 0` when the degree-one cohomology vanishes. -/
theorem h1_eq_zero [Nontrivial R] (h : Subsingleton (HModule F 1)) : h1 F = 0 :=
  haveI := h
  Module.finrank_zero_of_subsingleton

/-- `χ F = h⁰ F` when the degree-one cohomology vanishes. -/
theorem chi_eq_h0 [Nontrivial R] (h : Subsingleton (HModule F 1)) : chi F = h0 F := by
  rw [chi, h1_eq_zero h, Nat.cast_zero, sub_zero]

end CategoryTheory.Sheaf

21	`M` is chosen so that `deg (Θ^M) ≥ b` and the whole degree-`g` family lands in the vanishing
22	locus.

27	fiber divisor `F = fiberWeilDivisor π` and the base twist fixed at the FLV-fiber threshold `n₁` of

31	  `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(n·F))` for all `n ≥ n₁`; take `n = n₁`, so the base twist `n₁·F` is fixed;

34	  `exists_effective_of_picClass` yields an **effective** witness `E` of that class;
35	* `n₁·F + E` is in the class of `D`; `peel_effective` transports `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(n₁·F))` to

13	/-!
14	# FLV-4 — the class form and the remaining witnesses
15	
16	The final brick of the Wave-4 fibrewise-large-twist-vanishing campaign
17	(`informal/w4-flv-worksheet.md`, sub-brick FLV-4). It carries three obligations left open by
18	the FLV-2+3 landing (the vanishing headline `FLVVanishing.lean`):
19	
20	## 1. The surjectivity witness (`0 < deg (fiberWeilDivisor π)` unconditionally)
21	
22	`AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_of_isFinite_of_isDominant`: a finite dominant morphism is
23	surjective (a closed map with dense range hits everything). Feeding the surjection the
24	`ℙ¹`-point `[1 : 0]` (`P1.exists_mem_chartOpen_zero_notMem_one`, the origin of the chart
25	`D₊(X₀)` off the chart `D₊(X₁)`) produces a fiber point `x₀ ∈ V₀ ∖ V₁`, which discharges the
26	pole-existence witness of `AlgebraicGeometry.fiberWeilDivisor_deg_pos_of_notMem_chart₁`
27	unconditionally: `AlgebraicGeometry.zero_lt_deg_fiberWeilDivisor`, `0 < deg F`.
28	
29	## 2. The class form (`informal/w4-flv-worksheet.md` §§1.2, 2.5)
30	
31	`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_one_le_classDeg_of_isFinite_toP1`: for a
32	finite dominant `π : Y ⟶ ℙ¹` and any Čech Picard classes `l`, `θ` with `1 ≤ classDeg θ`, the
33	degree-one cohomology of `𝒪(D)` vanishes for **every** divisor `D` of class `l · θⁿ`, for all
34	large `n`. The reduction of the worksheet §2.5, in the simplified `m = m₀` form:
35	
36	* run FLV-fiber (`subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isFinite_toP1`) on a divisor `D₀`
37	  realizing `l`: `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(D₀ + m₀·F))`, `F` the fiber divisor, `d' := deg F ≥ 1`;
38	* for `n` large, the residual class `θⁿ · (𝒪(F))⁻ᵐ⁰` has degree `≥ 1 − χ(𝒪)`, so the Riemann
39	  inequality (`riemann_inequality`) gives a nonzero global section, hence an **effective**
40	  witness `E` of that class (`exists_effective_of_picClass`);
41	* `D₀ + m₀·F + E` is in class `l · θⁿ`; peeling `E` point-by-point transports `Subsingleton`
42	  up the landed dévissage surjections (`peel_effective`, from `Sheaf.HModule.surjective_map_f`);
43	* witness-independence (W6-lite `subsingleton_hModule_one_of_picClass_eq`) upgrades the single
44	  witness `D₀ + m₀·F + E` to every `D` of the class.
45	
46	The rank corollary `AlgebraicGeometry.h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one` records the
47	CBC-3 anchor `h⁰(𝒪(D)) = deg D + χ(𝒪)` under the vanishing.
48	
49	Both statements above take the finite dominant map as an explicit hypothesis, matching the shape
50	of the landed FLV-fiber `subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isFinite_toP1`. The curve layer
51	`C_K` satisfies every abstract-bundle instance, so a consumer holding a finite dominant
52	`π : C_K ⟶ ℙ¹` applies the class form directly.
53	
54	## 3. Frontier: the dominance discharge for the *constructed* map
55	
56	Specializing the class form to the curve layer with **no** external map hypothesis would require
57	`IsDominant` for the `π` produced by `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.MapToP1.exists_isFinite_toP1`. That
58	map is dominant (its construction sends the generic point to the generic point via transcendence),
59	but the fact is internal to `Curve/RationalToP1.lean` and not exported; re-deriving it from the
60	exported `IsFinite π` alone needs the stalk-integrality/transcendence argument
61	(`𝒪_{ℙ¹,π(η)} → K(C)` finite and `K(C)` a field force `𝒪_{ℙ¹,π(η)}` to be a field, i.e. `π(η)`
62	generic), which lives outside this brick's write scope (the landed `Curve/` files). Deferred; the
63	consumer supplies `[IsDominant π]` with the finite map it already constructs for the fiber
64	geometry.
65	-/

67	set_option autoImplicit false

71	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace MvPolynomial HomogeneousLocalization

77	/-! ## Divisor-bound comparison (public re-derivation) -/
78	
79	section Bound
80	
81	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
82	  [IsIntegral X]
83	
84	/-- The divisor-bound comparison at a point reduces to the pointwise coefficient comparison in
85	`ℤ`: `divisorBound A ≤ divisorBound B ↔ coeffAt A ≤ coeffAt B`. (Public re-derivation of the
86	`divisorBound`/`coeffAt` translation used across the fiber toolkit.) -/
87	lemma divisorBound_le_iff {A B : X.CurveDivisor} {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) :
88	    Scheme.divisorBound A hx ≤ Scheme.divisorBound B hx ↔
89	      coeffAt hx A ≤ coeffAt hx B := by
90	  simp only [Scheme.divisorBound, WithZero.coe_le_coe, Multiplicative.ofAdd_le]
91	  rfl
92	
93	end Bound
94	
95	/-! ## Class arithmetic -/
96	
97	section ClassArith
98	
99	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
100	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
101	  [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
102	
103	/-- The Čech Picard class of a multiple divisor is the power of the class:
104	`𝒪(n·D) = 𝒪(D)ⁿ`. -/
105	lemma picClass_nsmul (D : X.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ) :
106	    CurveDivisor.picClass K (n • D) = CurveDivisor.picClass K D ^ n := by
107	  induction n with
108	  | zero => rw [zero_nsmul, pow_zero, CurveDivisor.picClass_zero]
109	  | succ n ih => rw [succ_nsmul, CurveDivisor.picClass_add, ih, pow_succ]
110	
111	variable [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
112	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]
113	
114	/-- The degree of a power of a Čech Picard class is the multiple of the degree:
115	`classDeg (Lⁿ) = n · classDeg L`. -/
116	lemma classDeg_pow (L : X.CechPic) (n : ℕ) :
117	    classDeg K (L ^ n) = n * classDeg K L := by
118	  induction n with
119	  | zero => rw [pow_zero, classDeg_one, Nat.cast_zero, zero_mul]
120	  | succ n ih => rw [pow_succ, classDeg_mul, ih, Nat.cast_succ]; ring
121	
122	end ClassArith
123	
124	/-! ## The surjectivity witness (`0 < deg F`) -/
125	
126	section Witness
127	
128	/-- **A `ℙ¹`-point off the chart `D₊(X₁)`.** The origin `[1 : 0]` of the chart `D₊(X₀)`: the
129	prime containing the chart coordinate `X₁/X₀` (a non-unit — it is the polynomial variable),
130	whose image lies in `D₊(X₀)` but not in `D₊(X₁)`. This is the point whose (nonempty, by
131	surjectivity) fiber supplies the pole witness of the fiber divisor. -/
132	theorem exists_mem_chartOpen_zero_notMem_one (k : Type u) [Field k] :
133	    ∃ z : P1 k, z ∈ P1.chartOpen k 0 ∧ z ∉ P1.chartOpen k 1 := by
134	  have hpre : (P1.chartι k 0) ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1
135	      = PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen (P1.chartCoord k 0 1) := by
136	    change (Proj.awayι (homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k) (X 0) (P1.X_mem k 0) one_pos)
137	        ⁻¹ᵁ Proj.basicOpen (homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k) (X 1) = _
138	    rw [Proj.awayι_preimage_basicOpen (homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k)
139	        (P1.X_mem k 0) one_pos (P1.X_mem k 1) one_pos,
140	      P1.isLocalizationElem_X_eq k 0 1]
141	  have hnu : ¬ IsUnit (P1.chartCoord k 0 1) := by
142	    intro h
143	    have h2 := h.map (P1.awayAlgEquiv k P1.fin_zero_ne_one)
144	    rw [P1.awayAlgEquiv_chartCoord] at h2
145	    exact Polynomial.not_isUnit_X h2
146	  have hspan : Ideal.span {P1.chartCoord k 0 1} ≠ ⊤ := by
147	    rw [Ne, Ideal.span_singleton_eq_top]; exact hnu
148	  obtain ⟨M, hM, hle⟩ := Ideal.exists_le_maximal _ hspan
149	  have hpmem : P1.chartCoord k 0 1 ∈ M := hle (Ideal.mem_span_singleton_self _)
150	  refine ⟨(P1.chartι k 0).base ⟨M, hM.isPrime⟩, ?_, ?_⟩
151	  · rw [← P1.opensRange_chartι k 0]
152	    exact ⟨⟨M, hM.isPrime⟩, rfl⟩
153	  · intro hz
154	    have hmem : (⟨M, hM.isPrime⟩ :
155	        PrimeSpectrum (Away (homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k) (X 0)))
156	        ∈ (P1.chartι k 0) ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1 := hz
157	    rw [hpre] at hmem
158	    exact (PrimeSpectrum.mem_basicOpen _ _).mp hmem hpmem
159	
160	/-- **A finite dominant morphism is surjective.** Finiteness makes `π` a closed map, so its
161	range is closed; dominance makes the range dense; a closed dense set is everything. -/
162	theorem surjective_of_isFinite_of_isDominant {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (π : X ⟶ Y)
163	    [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π] : Function.Surjective π.base := by
164	  have hclosed : IsClosed (Set.range π.base) := π.isClosedMap.isClosed_range
165	  haveI : Surjective π := surjective_of_isDominant_of_isClosed_range π hclosed
166	  exact π.surjective
167	
168	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral Y]
169	  [Y.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
170	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
171	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
172	  [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
173	
174	/-- **The pole-existence witness, unconditional.** For a **finite** dominant `π : Y ⟶ ℙ¹`, the
175	fiber divisor `F = fiberWeilDivisor π` has strictly positive degree: surjectivity of `π` (finite
176	dominant) produces a point `x₀` over `[1 : 0] ∈ V₀ ∖ V₁`, discharging the fiber witness of
177	`AlgebraicGeometry.fiberWeilDivisor_deg_pos_of_notMem_chart₁`. This is the FLV-4 obligation that
178	frees the fibrewise vanishing from its pole-existence hypothesis. -/
179	theorem zero_lt_deg_fiberWeilDivisor (π : Y ⟶ P1 K) [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π] :
180	    0 < CurveDivisor.deg K (fiberWeilDivisor π) := by
181	  obtain ⟨z, hz0, hz1⟩ := exists_mem_chartOpen_zero_notMem_one K
182	  obtain ⟨x₀, hx₀⟩ := surjective_of_isFinite_of_isDominant π z
183	  have hxV₀ : x₀ ∈ fiberChart₀ π := by
184	    change π.base x₀ ∈ P1.chartOpen K 0; rw [hx₀]; exact hz0
185	  have hxV₁ : x₀ ∉ fiberChart₁ π := by
186	    change ¬ π.base x₀ ∈ P1.chartOpen K 1; rw [hx₀]; exact hz1
187	  have hx₀η : x₀ ≠ genericPoint Y := fun h =>
188	    hxV₁ (by rw [h]; exact (genericPoint_mem_preimage_inf π).2)
189	  exact fiberWeilDivisor_deg_pos_of_notMem_chart₁ π hx₀η hxV₀ hxV₁
190	
191	end Witness
192	
193	/-! ## The effective witness -/
194	
195	section Effective
196	
197	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
198	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
199	  [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
200	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
201	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]
202	
203	/-- **An effective witness of a class of large degree.** If a Weil divisor `W` has
204	`1 ≤ deg W + χ(𝒪)` then its Čech Picard class is realized by an **effective** divisor. The
205	Riemann inequality (`riemann_inequality`) forces a nonzero global section `f` of `𝒪(W)`, i.e.
206	`f ∈ K(X)ˣ` with `W + div f ≥ 0`; that shift is effective and of the same class
207	(`CurveDivisor.picClass_divOf`). -/
208	lemma exists_effective_of_picClass (W : X.CurveDivisor)
209	    (hW : 1 ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K W + Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K)) :
210	    ∃ E : X.CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ E ∧ CurveDivisor.picClass K E = CurveDivisor.picClass K W := by
211	  -- `h⁰(𝒪(W)) ≥ 1`, so `H⁰` is nontrivial.
212	  have hfr : 0 < Module.finrank K (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K W) 0) := by
213	    have h1 : (1 : ℤ) ≤ (Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K W) : ℤ) :=
214	      le_trans hW (riemann_inequality K W)
215	    have : 0 < Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K W) := by omega
216	    exact this
217	  haveI : Nontrivial (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K W) 0) :=
218	    Module.nontrivial_of_finrank_pos hfr
219	  -- a nonzero global section `g ∈ 𝒪(W)(⊤) ⊆ K(X)`.
220	  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := exists_ne (0 : Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K W) 0)
221	  set s := (Sheaf.HModule.linearEquiv₀ (Opens.grothendieckTopology (X : TopCat))
222	    (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens)) (X.divisorSheaf K W)) t with hs
223	  have hsne : s ≠ 0 := by
224	    rw [hs]; exact (LinearEquiv.map_ne_zero_iff _).mpr ht
225	  set g : X.functionField := divisorVal K s with hg
226	  have hgmem : g ∈ divisorSections K W ⊤ := divisorVal_mem K s
227	  have hgne : g ≠ 0 := by
228	    intro h
229	    exact hsne (divisorSection_ext K
230	      (show divisorVal K s = divisorVal K (0 : _) from by rw [← hg, h]; rfl))
231	  -- the unit `u` and the effective shift.
232	  set u : X.functionFieldˣ := Units.mk0 g hgne with hu
233	  have huval : (u : X.functionField) = g := rfl
234	  refine ⟨W + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) u, ?_, ?_⟩
235	  · -- effectivity: `coeffAt (W + div u) ≥ 0` from the pole bound
236	    refine Finsupp.le_def.mpr (fun p => ?_)
237	    change (0 : ℤ) ≤ coeffAt p.2 (W + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) u)
238	    have htop : ((⊤ : X.Opens) : Set X).Nonempty := ⟨genericPoint X, trivial⟩
239	    have hb := (mem_divisorSections_of_nonempty K htop).mp hgmem p.1 p.2 trivial
240	    rw [← huval, Scheme.ord_val_eq K u p.2, divisorBound_le_iff p.2,
241	      CurveDivisor.coeffAt_neg] at hb
242	    rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add]
243	    omega
244	  · -- same class
245	    rw [CurveDivisor.picClass_add, CurveDivisor.picClass_divOf, mul_one]
246	
247	end Effective
248	
249	/-! ## Effective peeling of `Subsingleton H¹` -/
250	
251	section Peel
252	
253	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
254	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
255	  [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
256	
257	/-- **Peeling one point.** Vanishing of `H¹(𝒪(B))` transports to `H¹(𝒪(B + x))` along the
258	landed dévissage surjection `H¹(𝒪(B)) ↠ H¹(𝒪(B + x))` (`Sheaf.HModule.surjective_map_f` on
259	`devissageSES`, whose skyscraper cokernel has vanishing `H¹`). -/
260	lemma peel_single {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (B : X.CurveDivisor)
261	    (h : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K B) 1)) :
262	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K (B + CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) 1) := by
263	  set D : X.CurveDivisor := B + CurveDivisor.single hx 1 with hD
264	  have hBD : devissageDivisor hx D = B := by rw [devissageDivisor_eq_sub, hD]; abel
265	  haveI : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₃ 1) :=
266	    skyModule_subsingleton_hModule_one x (jumpModule K hx D)
267	  have hsurj := Sheaf.HModule.surjective_map_f (devissageSES_shortExact K hx D) 1
268	  have hsub : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K (devissageDivisor hx D)) 1) := by
269	    rw [hBD]; exact h
270	  refine ⟨fun a b => ?_⟩
271	  obtain ⟨a', rfl⟩ := hsurj a
272	  obtain ⟨b', rfl⟩ := hsurj b
273	  exact congrArg _ (hsub.elim a' b')
274	
275	/-- **Peeling a multiple of a point.** Iterating `peel_single`: `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(A))`
276	transports to `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(A + n·x))`. -/
277	lemma peel_nsmul_single {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (A : X.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ)
278	    (h : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K A) 1)) :
279	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K (A + n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) 1) := by
280	  induction n with
281	  | zero => simpa using h
282	  | succ n ih =>
283	    have hstep := peel_single hx (A + n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1) ih
284	    have heq : A + n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1 + CurveDivisor.single hx 1
285	        = A + (n + 1) • CurveDivisor.single hx 1 := by
286	      rw [succ_nsmul]; abel
287	    rwa [heq] at hstep
288	
289	/-- **Effective peeling.** Vanishing of `H¹(𝒪(A))` transports to `H¹(𝒪(A + E))` for any
290	effective divisor `E`: peel the finitely many points of `E` one multiplicity-block at a time,
291	by induction on the size of the support. -/
292	lemma peel_effective (A E : X.CurveDivisor) (hE : 0 ≤ E)
293	    (h : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K A) 1)) :
294	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K (A + E)) 1) := by
295	  suffices H : ∀ (n : ℕ) (E : X.CurveDivisor), 0 ≤ E →
296	      (toFinsupp E).support.card = n →
297	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K (A + E)) 1) from H _ E hE rfl
298	  intro n
299	  induction n with
300	  | zero =>
301	    intro E hE hc
302	    have hE0 : E = 0 :=
303	      Finsupp.support_eq_empty.mp (Finset.card_eq_zero.mp hc)
304	    rw [hE0, add_zero]; exact h
305	  | succ n ih =>
306	    intro E hE hc
307	    classical
308	    have hne : (toFinsupp E).support.Nonempty := by
309	      rw [← Finset.card_pos, hc]; exact Nat.succ_pos n
310	    obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := hne
311	    set b : ℤ := toFinsupp E p with hb
312	    have hb_nonneg : 0 ≤ b := Finsupp.le_def.mp hE p
313	    have hbpos : 0 < b := lt_of_le_of_ne hb_nonneg (Ne.symm (Finsupp.mem_support_iff.mp hp))
314	    set E' : X.CurveDivisor := Finsupp.erase p (toFinsupp E) with hE'
315	    have hdecomp : CurveDivisor.single p.2 b + E' = E := by
316	      rw [hE', hb]
317	      exact Finsupp.single_add_erase p (toFinsupp E)
318	    have hE'nonneg : 0 ≤ E' := by
319	      rw [hE']
320	      refine Finsupp.le_def.mpr (fun q => ?_)
321	      by_cases hq : q = p
322	      · subst hq; rw [Finsupp.erase_same]; rfl
323	      · rw [Finsupp.erase_ne hq]; exact Finsupp.le_def.mp hE q
324	    have hcard : (toFinsupp E').support.card = n := by
325	      have hEF : toFinsupp E' = Finsupp.erase p (toFinsupp E) := rfl
326	      rw [hEF, Finsupp.support_erase, Finset.card_erase_of_mem hp, hc, Nat.succ_sub_one]
327	    have hrec := ih E' hE'nonneg hcard
328	    have hsingle : CurveDivisor.single p.2 b = b.toNat • CurveDivisor.single p.2 1 := by
329	      rw [CurveDivisor.nsmul_single_one, Int.toNat_of_nonneg hb_nonneg]
330	    have hsplit : A + E = (A + E') + b.toNat • CurveDivisor.single p.2 1 := by
331	      rw [← hdecomp, ← hsingle]; abel
332	    rw [hsplit]
333	    exact peel_nsmul_single p.2 (A + E') b.toNat hrec
334	
335	end Peel

337	/-! ## The class form -/
338	
339	section ClassForm
340	
341	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral Y]

9	# DD-0 — the section bound `h⁰(𝒪(A)) ≤ max 0 (deg A + 1)`
10	
11	The section-bound half of the DAT-D brick DD-0 (`informal/dat-d-worksheet.md` §5 DD-0,
12	consumed by the P-fib normalization step F1 of §3.3): on the curve bundle `X` (integral,
13	smooth of relative dimension one, quasi-compact over a field `K`, with finite `H⁰`/`H¹`
14	of `𝒪_X`), the global-section count of any divisor sheaf is bounded by its degree,
15	
16	`h⁰(𝒪(A)) ≤ max 0 (deg A + h⁰(𝒪_X))`,
17	
18	hence `≤ max 0 (deg A + 1)` when `h⁰(𝒪_X) = 1` (the geometrically-integral curve value,
19	`ChiCurve.h0_moduleKSheaf`; kept as an explicit hypothesis here so the ledger layer stays
20	on the abstract bundle).
21	
22	## Route (worksheet §5 DD-0: "peeling on the landed slice SES; base case via
23	effective-witness degree ≥ 0")
24	
25	* **`h¹` never drops under effective twists** (`h1_add_single_le` →
26	  `h1_add_effective_le`): the dévissage SES `0 → 𝒪(D − x) → 𝒪(D) → sky → 0` has
27	  skyscraper cokernel with no `H¹`, so the slice machinery
28	  (`Sheaf.HModule.surjective_map_f`, `ChiSlice.lean`) gives a surjection
29	  `H¹(𝒪(D − x)) ↠ H¹(𝒪(D))`; peel point by point exactly as `peel_effective`
30	  (`FLVClass.lean`). In particular `h¹(𝒪(E)) ≤ h¹(𝒪_X)` for `E ≥ 0`
31	  (`h1_le_of_effective`).
32	* **The effective witness** (`exists_effective_of_h0_pos`): a nonzero global section of
33	  `𝒪(A)` is a rational function `g` with `A + div g ≥ 0`, an *effective* divisor of the
34	  same class — the extraction of `exists_effective_of_picClass` run from `0 < h⁰`
35	  directly (no Riemann inequality needed). This is the base case: `0 < h⁰ ⟹ deg A ≥ 0`.
36	* **Assembly** (`h0_le_deg_add_h0_of_pos`, keystone `h0_divisorSheaf_le_max`): if
37	  `h⁰(𝒪(A)) > 0`, replace `A` by the effective witness `E` (class-invariance of `h⁰` and
38	  `deg`, `ClassCohomology`/`Degree`), then the χ-ledger `chi_divisorSheaf` reads
39	  `h⁰(𝒪(E)) = χ(𝒪_X) + deg E + h¹(𝒪(E)) ≤ deg A + h⁰(𝒪_X)`.
40	
41	The `h¹`-monotonicity lemmas are exported (not private): F1's window comparisons reuse
42	them, and they are the natural `H¹`-side companion of `peel_effective`.
43	-/

      eqToHom ((skyModule_obj_of_mem' M hU).trans (skyModule_obj_of_mem' M hV).symm) := by
  change (skyscraperSheaf x M).obj.map i = _

omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X] in
/-- Sections of `skyModule x M` over an open avoiding `x` form a subsingleton (terminal). -/
lemma skyModule_obj_subsingleton (M : ModuleCat.{u} K) {V : X.Opens} (hV : x ∉ V) :
    Subsingleton ((skyModule x M).obj.obj (op V)) := by
  rw [skyModule_obj_of_not_mem x M hV]
  exact ModuleCat.subsingleton_of_isZero terminalIsTerminal.isZero

variable (K)

/-- **The component of `π` over an open `W` (opposite-indexed).** On `unop W ∋ x` it is the
quotient projection `jumpProj` (landed in the skyscraper value `M` via the sealed `eqToHom`); on
`unop W ∌ x` it is the zero map into the terminal (zero) sections. -/
noncomputable def skyComponent (W : (X.Opens)ᵒᵖ) :
    (divisorPresheaf K D).obj W ⟶ (skyModule x (jumpModule K hx D)).obj.obj W :=
  if h : x ∈ unop W then
    ModuleCat.ofHom (jumpProj K hx D (unop W) h) ≫
      eqToHom (skyModule_obj_of_mem' (jumpModule K hx D) h).symm
  else 0

lemma skyComponent_of_mem (W : (X.Opens)ᵒᵖ) (hxW : x ∈ unop W) :
    skyComponent K hx D W =
      ModuleCat.ofHom (jumpProj K hx D (unop W) hxW) ≫
        eqToHom (skyModule_obj_of_mem' (jumpModule K hx D) hxW).symm := by
  rw [skyComponent]
  exact dif_pos hxW

/-- Element behaviour of `skyComponent` over `unop W ∋ x`: it is `jumpProj` followed by the
skyscraper `eqToHom` identification. -/
lemma skyComponent_hom_apply_of_mem (W : (X.Opens)ᵒᵖ) (hxW : x ∈ unop W)
    (s : (divisorPresheaf K D).obj W) :
    (skyComponent K hx D W).hom s =
      (eqToHom (skyModule_obj_of_mem' (jumpModule K hx D) hxW).symm).hom
        (jumpProj K hx D (unop W) hxW s) := by
  rw [skyComponent_of_mem K hx D W hxW]
  rfl

omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X] in
/-- The skyscraper restriction map, precomposed with the `eqToHom` identification at `U`, is the
`eqToHom` identification at `V` (both opens containing `x`). Sealed consequence of
`skyModule_map_eq`. -/
lemma eqToHom_comp_skyModule_map (M : ModuleCat.{u} K) {U V : (X.Opens)ᵒᵖ} (i : U ⟶ V)
    (hU : x ∈ unop U) (hV : x ∈ unop V) :
    eqToHom (skyModule_obj_of_mem' M hU).symm ≫ (skyModule x M).obj.map i
      = eqToHom (skyModule_obj_of_mem' M hV).symm := by
  rw [skyModule_map_eq M i hU hV, eqToHom_trans]

/-- **The presheaf morphism `π` underlying the skyscraper map.** -/
noncomputable def devissagePresheafπ :
    divisorPresheaf K D ⟶ (skyModule x (jumpModule K hx D)).obj where
  app W := skyComponent K hx D W
  naturality := by
    intro U V i
    by_cases hV : x ∈ unop V
    · have hU : x ∈ unop U := leOfHom i.unop hV
      apply ModuleCat.hom_ext
      apply LinearMap.ext
      intro s
      change (skyComponent K hx D V).hom (((divisorPresheaf K D).map i).hom s)
        = ((skyModule x (jumpModule K hx D)).obj.map i).hom ((skyComponent K hx D U).hom s)
      rw [skyComponent_hom_apply_of_mem K hx D V hV, skyComponent_hom_apply_of_mem K hx D U hU]
      have hjump : jumpProj K hx D (unop V) hV (((divisorPresheaf K D).map i).hom s)
          = jumpProj K hx D (unop U) hU s := by
        refine jumpProj_eq_of_coe_eq K hx D hV hU _ s ?_
        exact divisorSectionsRes_coe K (leOfHom i.unop) ⟨x, hV⟩ s
      rw [hjump]
      exact (LinearMap.congr_fun (congrArg ModuleCat.Hom.hom
        (eqToHom_comp_skyModule_map K (jumpModule K hx D) i hU hV))
        (jumpProj K hx D (unop U) hU s)).symm
    · apply ModuleCat.hom_ext
      apply LinearMap.ext
      intro s
      haveI := skyModule_obj_subsingleton (jumpModule K hx D) hV
      exact Subsingleton.elim _ _

/-- **The dévissage skyscraper morphism** `π : 𝒪(D) ⟶ sky_x J` of sheaves of `K`-modules,
sending a section `g` over `U ∋ x` to its class `⟦g⟧` in the jump module (and to `0` away from
`x`). -/
noncomputable def devissageπ :
    divisorSheaf K D ⟶ skyModule x (jumpModule K hx D) :=
  (fullyFaithfulSheafToPresheaf _ _).preimage (devissagePresheafπ K hx D)

lemma devissageπ_hom :
    (devissageπ K hx D).hom = devissagePresheafπ K hx D :=
  (fullyFaithfulSheafToPresheaf _ _).map_preimage
    (X := divisorSheaf K D) (Y := skyModule x (jumpModule K hx D)) (devissagePresheafπ K hx D)

/-- The component of `π` over an open `W` is `skyComponent`. -/
lemma devissageπ_app (W : (X.Opens)ᵒᵖ) :
    (devissageπ K hx D).hom.app W = skyComponent K hx D W := by
  rw [devissageπ_hom]; rfl

`⟦s⟧`, transported into the skyscraper value via the sealed `eqToHom`. -/

theorem injective_map_f_zero (hS : S.ShortExact) :

(exactness at `Hⁿ(X₂)` plus triviality of the next term). -/
theorem surjective_map_f (hS : S.ShortExact) (n : ℕ) [Subsingleton (HModule S.X₃ n)] :
    Function.Surjective (map S.f n) := fun y =>

section FinitenessTransfer

variable {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
  {R : Type u} [Field R] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} R)]
  {S : ShortComplex (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R))}

/-- **Finiteness of the middle cohomology**: if `Hⁿ(X₁)` and `Hⁿ(X₃)` are finite, so is
`Hⁿ(X₂)` (extension lemma along the exact slice). -/
theorem moduleFinite_middle (hS : S.ShortExact) (n : ℕ)
    [Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₁ n)] [Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₃ n)] :
    Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₂ n) :=
  FiniteDimensional.of_exact (map S.f n) (map S.g n) (exact_map_f_map_g hS n)

/-- **Finiteness of the left cohomology in degree zero**: `H⁰(X₁)` embeds in `H⁰(X₂)`, so
finiteness descends. -/
theorem moduleFinite_left_zero (hS : S.ShortExact) [Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₂ 0)] :
    Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₁ 0) :=
  FiniteDimensional.of_injective (map S.f 0) (injective_map_f_zero hS)

/-- **Finiteness of the left cohomology in positive degree**: `Hⁿ¹(X₁)` is an extension of
a submodule of the finite `Hⁿ¹(X₂)` by the image of the finite `Hⁿ⁰(X₃)` (exactness of the
slice at `Hⁿ¹(X₁)`). -/
theorem moduleFinite_left_succ (hS : S.ShortExact) {n₀ n₁ : ℕ} (h : n₀ + 1 = n₁)
    [Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₃ n₀)] [Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₂ n₁)] :
    Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₁ n₁) :=
  FiniteDimensional.of_exact (delta hS h) (map S.f n₁) (exact_delta_map_f hS h)

end FinitenessTransfer

/-- **Additivity of the Euler characteristic** along a short exact sequence of sheaves of
`R`-modules whose third term has vanishing `H¹`: `χ X₂ = χ X₁ + χ X₃`. This is the
alternating-sum identity for the five-term exact slice
`0 → H⁰X₁ → H⁰X₂ → H⁰X₃ → H¹X₁ → H¹X₂ → 0`. -/
theorem chi_eq_add_of_shortExact (hS : S.ShortExact)
    [Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₁ 0)] [Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₂ 0)]
    [Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₃ 0)] [Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₁ 1)]
    [Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₂ 1)] [Subsingleton (HModule S.X₃ 1)] :
    chi S.X₂ = chi S.X₁ + chi S.X₃ := by
  have hone : (0 : ℕ) + 1 = 1 := rfl
  have halt := AlgebraicGeometry.finrank_alt_sum_eq_zero_of_exact₅
    (HModule.map S.f 0) (HModule.map S.g 0) (HModule.delta hS hone) (HModule.map S.f 1)
    (HModule.injective_map_f_zero hS) (HModule.exact_map_f_map_g hS 0)
    (HModule.exact_map_g_delta hS hone) (HModule.exact_delta_map_f hS hone)
    (HModule.surjective_map_f hS 1)
  have h3 : h1 S.X₃ = 0 := h1_eq_zero inferInstance
  rw [chi, chi, chi, h3]
  unfold h0 h1
  omega

end ChiAdditivity

end CategoryTheory.Sheaf

import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Chi
import AlgebraicJacobian.Algebra.DedekindColength

/-!
# The six-term cohomology slice of a short exact sequence of sheaves

For a short exact sequence `0 ⟶ X₁ ⟶ X₂ ⟶ X₃ ⟶ 0` of sheaves of `R`-modules on a small
site, this file packages — **once, and elementwise** — the degree-`≤ 1` slice of the long
exact cohomology sequence

    0 → H⁰X₁ → H⁰X₂ → H⁰X₃ →δ→ H¹X₁ → H¹X₂ → H¹X₃

obtained from mathlib's covariant `Ext`-sequence for the cohomology carrier
`Sheaf.HModule = Ext(constModuleSheaf, ·)`: the connecting map `HModule.delta`, the four
`Function.Exact` facts, injectivity at the left end and surjectivity of `H¹X₁ → H¹X₂`
when `H¹X₃` vanishes.

On top of the slice sit the two consumers of the χ-ledger:

* **finiteness transfer** (`HModule.moduleFinite_middle`, `moduleFinite_left_zero`,
  `moduleFinite_left_succ`): dimension bookkeeping between the terms of the sequence,
  via the division-ring extension lemma `FiniteDimensional.of_exact`;
* **additivity of χ** (`Sheaf.chi_eq_add_of_shortExact`): when `H¹X₃ = 0` and the five
  remaining modules are finite, `χ X₂ = χ X₁ + χ X₃` — the alternating-sum identity
  `AlgebraicGeometry.finrank_alt_sum_eq_zero_of_exact₅` applied to the slice.

The transports from mathlib's `(mk₀ f).postcomp`-spelling to `HModule.map` are definitional
(`Ext`-postcomposition on both sides); each slot of the slice is nevertheless a named
lemma, so downstream files never re-derive the sequence inline.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite

section FiniteDimensional

variable {K V₁ V₂ V₃ : Type*} [DivisionRing K]
  [AddCommGroup V₁] [Module K V₁] [AddCommGroup V₂] [Module K V₂]
  [AddCommGroup V₃] [Module K V₃]

/-- **Extension lemma for finite dimensionality.** If `V₁ → V₂ → V₃` is exact at `V₂` and
the outer terms are finite-dimensional, so is the middle: the kernel of `V₂ → V₃` is the
image of the finite `V₁`, and the coimage embeds into the finite `V₃`. (Mathlib's
`Module.Finite.of_exact` asks for surjectivity of the second map; over a division ring the
corestriction to the range removes that hypothesis.) -/
theorem FiniteDimensional.of_exact (f : V₁ →ₗ[K] V₂) (g : V₂ →ₗ[K] V₃)
    (h : Function.Exact f g) [FiniteDimensional K V₁] [FiniteDimensional K V₃] :
    FiniteDimensional K V₂ := by
  have hexact : Function.Exact f g.rangeRestrict := fun y => by
    rw [← h y]
    exact ⟨fun hy => congrArg Subtype.val hy, fun hy => Subtype.ext hy⟩
  exact Module.Finite.of_exact hexact g.surjective_rangeRestrict

end FiniteDimensional

namespace CategoryTheory.Sheaf

variable {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
  {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} R)]
  {S : ShortComplex (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R))}

namespace HModule

/-- **The connecting homomorphism** `δ : Hⁿ⁰(X₃) →ₗ[R] Hⁿ¹(X₁)` (`n₀ + 1 = n₁`) of a short
exact sequence of sheaves of `R`-modules: postcomposition with the extension class of the
sequence. -/
noncomputable def delta (hS : S.ShortExact) {n₀ n₁ : ℕ} (h : n₀ + 1 = n₁) :
    HModule S.X₃ n₀ →ₗ[R] HModule S.X₁ n₁ :=
  hS.extClass.postcompOfLinear R (constModuleSheaf J R) h

/-- Exactness of `Hⁿ(X₁) → Hⁿ(X₂) → Hⁿ(X₃)` at `Hⁿ(X₂)`, elementwise
(`Abelian.Ext.covariant_sequence_exact₂'` transported to `HModule.map`). -/
theorem exact_map_f_map_g (hS : S.ShortExact) (n : ℕ) :
    Function.Exact (map S.f n) (map S.g n) := by
  have h := Abelian.Ext.covariant_sequence_exact₂' (constModuleSheaf J R) hS n
  rw [ShortComplex.ab_exact_iff_function_exact] at h
  exact h

/-- Exactness of `Hⁿ⁰(X₂) → Hⁿ⁰(X₃) →δ→ Hⁿ¹(X₁)` at `Hⁿ⁰(X₃)`, elementwise
(`Abelian.Ext.covariant_sequence_exact₃'` transported to `HModule.map`/`HModule.delta`). -/
theorem exact_map_g_delta (hS : S.ShortExact) {n₀ n₁ : ℕ} (h : n₀ + 1 = n₁) :
    Function.Exact (map S.g n₀) (delta hS h) := by
  have h' := Abelian.Ext.covariant_sequence_exact₃' (constModuleSheaf J R) hS n₀ n₁ h
  rw [ShortComplex.ab_exact_iff_function_exact] at h'
  exact h'

/-- Exactness of `Hⁿ⁰(X₃) →δ→ Hⁿ¹(X₁) → Hⁿ¹(X₂)` at `Hⁿ¹(X₁)`, elementwise
(`Abelian.Ext.covariant_sequence_exact₁'` transported to `HModule.map`/`HModule.delta`). -/
theorem exact_delta_map_f (hS : S.ShortExact) {n₀ n₁ : ℕ} (h : n₀ + 1 = n₁) :
    Function.Exact (delta hS h) (map S.f n₁) := by
  have h' := Abelian.Ext.covariant_sequence_exact₁' (constModuleSheaf J R) hS n₀ n₁ h
  rw [ShortComplex.ab_exact_iff_function_exact] at h'
  exact h'

/-- **Left end of the slice**: `H⁰(X₁) → H⁰(X₂)` is injective when `X₁ ⟶ X₂` is a
monomorphism (mathlib's `Abelian.Ext.postcomp_mk₀_injective_of_mono`). -/
theorem injective_map_f_zero (hS : S.ShortExact) :
    Function.Injective (map S.f 0) :=
  haveI := hS.mono_f
  Abelian.Ext.postcomp_mk₀_injective_of_mono (constModuleSheaf J R) S.f

/-- **Right end of the slice**: `Hⁿ(X₁) → Hⁿ(X₂)` is surjective when `Hⁿ(X₃)` vanishes
(exactness at `Hⁿ(X₂)` plus triviality of the next term). -/
theorem surjective_map_f (hS : S.ShortExact) (n : ℕ) [Subsingleton (HModule S.X₃ n)] :
    Function.Surjective (map S.f n) := fun y =>
  (exact_map_f_map_g hS n y).mp (Subsingleton.elim _ 0)

section FinitenessTransfer

variable {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
  {R : Type u} [Field R] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} R)]
  {S : ShortComplex (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R))}

/-- **Finiteness of the middle cohomology**: if `Hⁿ(X₁)` and `Hⁿ(X₃)` are finite, so is
`Hⁿ(X₂)` (extension lemma along the exact slice). -/
theorem moduleFinite_middle (hS : S.ShortExact) (n : ℕ)
    [Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₁ n)] [Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₃ n)] :
    Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₂ n) :=
  FiniteDimensional.of_exact (map S.f n) (map S.g n) (exact_map_f_map_g hS n)

/-- **Finiteness of the left cohomology in degree zero**: `H⁰(X₁)` embeds in `H⁰(X₂)`, so
finiteness descends. -/
theorem moduleFinite_left_zero (hS : S.ShortExact) [Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₂ 0)] :
    Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₁ 0) :=
  FiniteDimensional.of_injective (map S.f 0) (injective_map_f_zero hS)

/-- **Finiteness of the left cohomology in positive degree**: `Hⁿ¹(X₁)` is an extension of
a submodule of the finite `Hⁿ¹(X₂)` by the image of the finite `Hⁿ⁰(X₃)` (exactness of the
slice at `Hⁿ¹(X₁)`). -/
theorem moduleFinite_left_succ (hS : S.ShortExact) {n₀ n₁ : ℕ} (h : n₀ + 1 = n₁)
    [Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₃ n₀)] [Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₂ n₁)] :
    Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₁ n₁) :=
  FiniteDimensional.of_exact (delta hS h) (map S.f n₁) (exact_delta_map_f hS h)

end FinitenessTransfer

end HModule

section ChiAdditivity

variable {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
  {R : Type u} [Field R] [HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} R)]
  {S : ShortComplex (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R))}

/-- **Additivity of the Euler characteristic** along a short exact sequence of sheaves of
`R`-modules whose third term has vanishing `H¹`: `χ X₂ = χ X₁ + χ X₃`. This is the
alternating-sum identity for the five-term exact slice
`0 → H⁰X₁ → H⁰X₂ → H⁰X₃ → H¹X₁ → H¹X₂ → 0`. -/
theorem chi_eq_add_of_shortExact (hS : S.ShortExact)
    [Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₁ 0)] [Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₂ 0)]
    [Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₃ 0)] [Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₁ 1)]
    [Module.Finite R (HModule S.X₂ 1)] [Subsingleton (HModule S.X₃ 1)] :
    chi S.X₂ = chi S.X₁ + chi S.X₃ := by
  have hone : (0 : ℕ) + 1 = 1 := rfl
  have halt := AlgebraicGeometry.finrank_alt_sum_eq_zero_of_exact₅
    (HModule.map S.f 0) (HModule.map S.g 0) (HModule.delta hS hone) (HModule.map S.f 1)
    (HModule.injective_map_f_zero hS) (HModule.exact_map_f_map_g hS 0)
    (HModule.exact_map_g_delta hS hone) (HModule.exact_delta_map_f hS hone)
    (HModule.surjective_map_f hS 1)
  have h3 : h1 S.X₃ = 0 := h1_eq_zero inferInstance
  rw [chi, chi, chi, h3]
  unfold h0 h1
  omega

end ChiAdditivity

end CategoryTheory.Sheaf

/-- The degree of a one-point divisor: `deg (n · x) = n · [κ(x) : K]`. -/
lemma Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_single' (K : Type u) [CommRing K]
    [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (n : ℤ) :
    CurveDivisor.deg K (CurveDivisor.single hx n) = n * X.residueDeg K x :=
  CurveDivisor.deg_single K (X := X) (⟨x, hx⟩ : {p : X // p ≠ genericPoint X}) n

/-- Single-bump induction for finitely supported `ℤ`-valued functions: a predicate that
holds at `0` and is invariant under adding a single generator holds everywhere. -/
private theorem finsupp_induction_bump {α : Type u} {P : (α →₀ ℤ) → Prop} (zero : P 0)
    (bump : ∀ (a : α) (f : α →₀ ℤ), P (f + Finsupp.single a 1) ↔ P f) (f : α →₀ ℤ) :
    P f := by
  have hn : ∀ (n : ℤ), ∀ (a : α) (f : α →₀ ℤ), P (f + Finsupp.single a n) ↔ P f := by
    intro n
    induction n using Int.induction_on with
    | zero => intro a f; rw [Finsupp.single_zero, add_zero]
    | succ n ih =>
      intro a f
      have h1 : f + Finsupp.single a ((n : ℤ) + 1) =
          f + Finsupp.single a (n : ℤ) + Finsupp.single a 1 := by
        rw [Finsupp.single_add, add_assoc]
      rw [h1, bump a (f + Finsupp.single a (n : ℤ)), ih a f]
    | pred n ih =>
      intro a f
      have h1 : f + Finsupp.single a (-(n : ℤ) - 1) + Finsupp.single a 1 =
          f + Finsupp.single a (-(n : ℤ)) := by
        rw [add_assoc, ← Finsupp.single_add]
        norm_num
      rw [← ih a f, ← bump a (f + Finsupp.single a (-(n : ℤ) - 1)), h1]
  induction f using Finsupp.induction with
  | zero => exact zero
  | single_add a b f _ _ ih =>
    rw [show Finsupp.single a b + f = f + Finsupp.single a b from add_comm _ _]
    exact (hn b a f).mpr ih

/-- **Dévissage induction on Weil divisors.** A predicate on `X.CurveDivisor` that holds
for the zero divisor and transfers (in both directions) along the one-point dévissage
`D ↭ devissageDivisor hx D = D − x` holds for every divisor. This is the induction
scaffolding shared by the finiteness dévissage and the χ-ledger `chi_divisorSheaf`. -/
theorem Scheme.CurveDivisor.induction_devissage {P : X.CurveDivisor → Prop} (zero : P 0)
    (step : ∀ {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (D : X.CurveDivisor),
      P D ↔ P (devissageDivisor hx D))
    (D : X.CurveDivisor) : P D := by
  refine finsupp_induction_bump (P := fun F : {p : X // p ≠ genericPoint X} →₀ ℤ => P F)
    zero (fun p F => ?_) D
  have h := step p.2 (F + Finsupp.single p 1)
  have h2 : P (devissageDivisor p.2 (F + Finsupp.single p 1)) ↔ P F := by
    have heq : devissageDivisor p.2 (F + Finsupp.single p 1) = (F : X.CurveDivisor) := by
      change F + Finsupp.single p 1 - Finsupp.single p 1 = F
      abel
    rw [heq]
  exact h.trans h2

/-- Adding the point back: `(D − x) + x = D` for the dévissage twist. -/
lemma devissageDivisor_add_single {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (D : X.CurveDivisor) :
    devissageDivisor hx D + CurveDivisor.single hx 1 = D := by
  rw [devissageDivisor_eq_sub]
  abel

/-- The degree drops by the residue degree along the dévissage twist:
`deg (D − x) = deg D − [κ(x) : K]`. -/
lemma deg_devissageDivisor (K : Type u) [CommRing K] [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (D : X.CurveDivisor) :
    CurveDivisor.deg K (devissageDivisor hx D) =
      CurveDivisor.deg K D - X.residueDeg K x := by
  have h := CurveDivisor.deg_add K (devissageDivisor hx D) (CurveDivisor.single hx 1)
  rw [devissageDivisor_add_single hx D] at h
  have hsingle : CurveDivisor.deg K (CurveDivisor.single hx 1) = X.residueDeg K x := by
    have h1 := CurveDivisor.deg_single K (X := X)
      (⟨x, hx⟩ : {p : X // p ≠ genericPoint X}) 1
    rw [one_mul] at h1
    exact h1
  rw [hsingle] at h
  omega

end Scaffolding

/-! ## The cohomology of a skyscraper is finite -/

section Skyscraper

variable {K : Type u} [CommRing K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]

/-- `H⁰` of a skyscraper sheaf with finite value module is a finite `K`-module
(transport of the value module along `skyModuleGammaEquiv`). -/
theorem moduleFinite_hModule_skyModule_zero (x : X) (M : ModuleCat.{u} K)
    [Module.Finite K M] :
    Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (skyModule x M) 0) :=
  Module.Finite.equiv (skyModuleGammaEquiv x M).symm

/-- `H¹` of a skyscraper sheaf is a finite `K`-module (it vanishes). -/
theorem moduleFinite_hModule_skyModule_one (x : X) (M : ModuleCat.{u} K) :
    Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (skyModule x M) 1) :=
  haveI : Finite (Sheaf.HModule (skyModule x M) 1) := Finite.of_subsingleton
  Module.Finite.of_finite

end Skyscraper

57	  rw [Sheaf.chi_eq_h0 (skyModule_subsingleton_hModule_one x M), h0_skyModule]
58	
59	end Skyscraper

61	/-! ## The ledger -/
62	
63	section Ledger
64	
65	variable (K : Type u) [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
66	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
67	  [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
68	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
69	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]
70	
71	/-- **The dévissage step of the χ-ledger** (★): subtracting a closed point `x` from the
72	divisor drops the Euler characteristic by the residue degree `[κ(x) : K]`:
73	`χ(𝒪(D)) = χ(𝒪(D − x)) + residueDeg x`. The divisor `D − CurveDivisor.single hx 1` is
74	definitionally the dévissage twist `devissageDivisor hx D` of the landed short exact
75	sequence (`devissageDivisor_eq_sub`). -/
76	theorem chi_step {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (D : X.CurveDivisor) :
77	    Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K D) =
78	      Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K (D - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) + X.residueDeg K x := by
79	  have hS := devissageSES_shortExact K hx D
80	  -- the five finiteness inputs and the `H¹(sky) = 0` input, in the `devissageSES` spelling
81	  haveI h₁0 : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₁ 0) :=
82	    moduleFinite_hModule_divisorSheaf_zero K (devissageDivisor hx D)
83	  haveI h₁1 : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₁ 1) :=
84	    moduleFinite_hModule_divisorSheaf_one K (devissageDivisor hx D)
85	  haveI h₂0 : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₂ 0) :=
86	    moduleFinite_hModule_divisorSheaf_zero K D
87	  haveI h₂1 : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₂ 1) :=
88	    moduleFinite_hModule_divisorSheaf_one K D
89	  haveI h₃0 : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₃ 0) :=
90	    haveI := moduleFinite_jumpModule K hx D
91	    moduleFinite_hModule_skyModule_zero x (jumpModule K hx D)
92	  haveI h₃1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₃ 1) :=
93	    skyModule_subsingleton_hModule_one x (jumpModule K hx D)
94	  have hadd := Sheaf.chi_eq_add_of_shortExact hS
95	  -- identify the three χ's with their divisor-sheaf/skyscraper spellings (definitional)
96	  have hX₂ : Sheaf.chi (devissageSES K hx D).X₂ = Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K D) := rfl
97	  have hX₁ : Sheaf.chi (devissageSES K hx D).X₁ =
98	      Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K (D - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) := rfl
99	  have hX₃ : Sheaf.chi (devissageSES K hx D).X₃ = (X.residueDeg K x : ℤ) := by
100	    have h := chi_skyModule x (jumpModule K hx D)
101	    rw [finrank_jumpModule K hx D] at h
102	    exact h
103	  rw [hX₂, hX₁, hX₃] at hadd
104	  exact hadd
105	
106	/-- **The χ-ledger, closed** (★): for every Weil divisor `D` on the curve bundle,
107	`χ(𝒪(D)) = χ(𝒪_X) + deg D`. Base case `𝒪(0) ≅ 𝒪_X`, step `chi_step`, glue
108	`CurveDivisor.induction_devissage`. -/
109	theorem chi_divisorSheaf (D : X.CurveDivisor) :
110	    Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K D) =
111	      Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) + CurveDivisor.deg K D := by
112	  refine Scheme.CurveDivisor.induction_devissage
113	    (P := fun D => Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K D) =
114	      Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) + CurveDivisor.deg K D)
115	    ?_ (fun {x} hx D => ?_) D
116	  · rw [Sheaf.chi_congr (divisorSheafZeroIso K), CurveDivisor.deg_zero, add_zero]
117	  · rw [devissageDivisor_eq_sub hx D]
118	    have hstep := chi_step K hx D
119	    have hdeg := deg_devissageDivisor K hx D
120	    rw [devissageDivisor_eq_sub hx D] at hdeg
121	    constructor <;> intro h <;> omega
122	
123	/-- **Principal divisors have degree zero**: `deg (div g) = 0` for a unit `g` of the
124	function field. Multiplication by `g` identifies `𝒪(0)` with `𝒪(0 − div g)`
125	(`mulEquivDivisorSheaf`), so the two sides of the χ-ledger force the degrees to agree. -/
126	theorem deg_divOf (g : X.functionFieldˣ) :
127	    CurveDivisor.deg K (Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) g) = 0 := by
128	  have hcongr := Sheaf.chi_congr (mulEquivDivisorSheaf K g (0 : X.CurveDivisor))
129	  rw [chi_divisorSheaf K (0 : X.CurveDivisor),
130	    chi_divisorSheaf K ((0 : X.CurveDivisor) - Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) g),
131	    CurveDivisor.deg_zero, zero_sub, CurveDivisor.deg_neg] at hcongr
132	  omega
133	
134	/-- **The Riemann inequality** (G9, general conditional form): for every Weil divisor `D`,
135	`deg D + χ(𝒪_X) ≤ h⁰(𝒪(D))` — from the χ-ledger and `h¹ ≥ 0`. The curve-level
136	`deg D + 1 − genus` form is derived in `ChiCurve`. -/
137	theorem riemann_inequality (D : X.CurveDivisor) :
138	    CurveDivisor.deg K D + Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) ≤
139	      (Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K D) : ℤ) := by
140	  have h := chi_divisorSheaf K D
141	  have hchi : Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K D) ≤ (Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K D) : ℤ) := by
142	    rw [Sheaf.chi]
143	    omega
144	  omega
145	
146	/-- **Unbounded growth of `h⁰` along multiples of a point** (G9): for every closed point
147	`x` and every bound `N` there is `n` with `N ≤ h⁰(𝒪(n · x))`. No rational point is
148	needed: `residueDeg x ≥ 1` suffices. -/
149	theorem h0_nsmul_point_unbounded {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (N : ℕ) :
150	    ∃ n : ℕ, N ≤ Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K (n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) := by
151	  have key : ∀ n : ℕ, (n : ℤ) - Sheaf.h1 (X.moduleKSheaf K) ≤
152	      (Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K (n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) : ℤ) := by
153	    intro n
154	    have hchi := chi_divisorSheaf K (n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1)
155	    rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.nsmul_single_one hx n,
156	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_single' K hx (n : ℤ)] at hchi
157	    have hchile : Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K (n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) ≤
158	        (Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K (n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) : ℤ) := by
159	      rw [Sheaf.chi]
160	      omega
161	    have hres : (1 : ℤ) ≤ (X.residueDeg K x : ℤ) := by
162	      exact_mod_cast Scheme.residueDeg_pos hx
163	    have hmul : (n : ℤ) * 1 ≤ (n : ℤ) * (X.residueDeg K x : ℤ) :=
164	      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hres (by positivity)
165	    have hchiO : Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) =
166	        (Sheaf.h0 (X.moduleKSheaf K) : ℤ) - Sheaf.h1 (X.moduleKSheaf K) := rfl
167	    -- `hchi` rewrote the divisor to `single hx n`; transport back is definitional
168	    have hchi' : Sheaf.chi (X.divisorSheaf K (n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) =
169	        Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K) + (n : ℤ) * (X.residueDeg K x : ℤ) := by
170	      rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.nsmul_single_one hx n]
171	      exact hchi
172	    omega
173	  refine ⟨N + Sheaf.h1 (X.moduleKSheaf K), ?_⟩
174	  have h := key (N + Sheaf.h1 (X.moduleKSheaf K))
175	  omega
176	
177	end Ledger
178	
179	end AlgebraicGeometry

11	/-!
12	# FLV-2(b) + FLV-3 — the H¹-quotient identification and the fibrewise large-twist vanishing
13	
14	The heart of the Wave-4 fibrewise-large-twist-vanishing campaign
15	(`informal/w4-flv-worksheet.md` §§2.1, 2.3, bricks FLV-2(b) and FLV-3), for the curve
16	bundle `Y` (integral, smooth of relative dimension one and quasi-compact over a field `K`)
17	with a dominant affine morphism `π : Y ⟶ ℙ¹` and its fiber divisor
18	`F = fiberWeilDivisor π` (`AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.FLVFiberToolkit`).
19	
20	## The identification (FLV-2(b))
21	
22	On the affine two-cover `V₀ = π⁻¹ D₊(X₀)`, `V₁ = π⁻¹ D₊(X₁)`, the general-coefficients
23	two-cover carrier `Scheme.twoCoverH1LinearEquiv` — its two affine vanishing instances
24	discharged by the quasi-coherence packaging of `AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.FLVQcoh` —
25	computes `H¹` of the twisted sheaf `𝒪(D + n·F)` as a cokernel of section modules. This
26	file identifies that cokernel with a quotient of the **fixed** ambient overlap lattice
27	`N = 𝒪(D)(V₀ ⊓ V₁)` (constant in `n`, by the landed overlap-constancy
28	`divisorSections_add_nsmul_fiberWeilDivisor_overlap`) by the fiber lattice `Aₙ` of
29	`AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.FLVLattice`, comapped through `N.subtype` — the one
30	submodule-of-submodule bridge of the campaign, paid once behind the named submodule
31	`AlgebraicGeometry.fiberLatticeOverlap` (worksheet discipline (2)):
32	
33	`AlgebraicGeometry.fiberLatticeH1Equiv :
34	  HModule (𝒪(D + n·F)) 1 ≃ₗ[K] N ⧸ fiberLatticeOverlap π D n`.
35	
36	## The endgame (FLV-3)
37	
38	`Submodule.eventually_eq_top_of_monotone_of_iSup_eq_top` is the pure linear-algebra
39	stabilization: an increasing `ℕ`-chain of submodules with join `⊤` whose base has
40	Noetherian quotient is eventually `⊤` (images in the quotient by the base stabilize by
41	`monotone_stabilizes_iff_noetherian`, and the stabilized value must be everything).
42	Instantiated with `Aₙ` inside `N`:
43	
44	* the chain is increasing (`fiberLattice_mono`) and exhausts `N` (`iSup_fiberLattice`,
45	  THE EXHAUSTION of FLV-1 — pole clearing at the finite fiber over `[1 : 0]`);
46	* `N ⧸ A₀` is finite-dimensional: it is `H¹(𝒪(D + 0·F))` through the identification, and
47	  every divisor sheaf has finite `H¹` by the landed dévissage
48	  (`moduleFinite_hModule_divisorSheaf_one`, `AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.ChiFiniteness`)
49	  — the only place the base finiteness (properness) inputs enter;
50	
51	so `Aₙ = ⊤` for all large `n`, and through the identification the twisted `H¹` is a
52	subsingleton — **the fibrewise large-twist vanishing**
53	(`AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isDominant_toP1`): per-class
54	`n₀`, no duality, no `R¹f_*`. The worksheet-shaped form for a finite dominant `π`
55	compatible with the structure morphisms
56	(`subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isFinite_toP1`) discharges the base
57	`H¹(𝒪_Y)`-finiteness input from finiteness of `π`
58	(`moduleFinite_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1`).
59	-/
60	
61	set_option autoImplicit false
62	
63	universe u v
64	
65	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace

67	section Stabilization
68	
69	/-- **Noetherian stabilization of an exhausting chain.** An increasing `ℕ`-chain of
70	submodules whose join is everything and whose base term has Noetherian quotient is
71	eventually everything: the images of the chain in the quotient by the base term stabilize,
72	and the stabilized image must be the whole quotient. This is the pure linear-algebra
73	endgame of the fibrewise large-twist vanishing (`informal/w4-flv-worksheet.md` §2.1). -/
74	theorem Submodule.eventually_eq_top_of_monotone_of_iSup_eq_top {R : Type u} {M : Type v}
75	    [Ring R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] {A : ℕ → Submodule R M} (hmono : Monotone A)
76	    (hsup : ⨆ n, A n = ⊤) [IsNoetherian R (M ⧸ A 0)] :
77	    ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ n₀, A n = ⊤ := by
78	  set f : ℕ →o Submodule R (M ⧸ A 0) :=
79	    ⟨fun n => (A n).map (A 0).mkQ, fun a b hab => Submodule.map_mono (hmono hab)⟩ with hf
80	  obtain ⟨n₀, hn₀⟩ :=
81	    monotone_stabilizes_iff_noetherian.mpr ‹IsNoetherian R (M ⧸ A 0)› f
82	  have hftop : f n₀ = ⊤ := by
83	    have h1 : ⨆ n, f n = ⊤ := by
84	      have h2 : ⨆ n, f n = Submodule.map (A 0).mkQ (⨆ n, A n) :=
85	        (Submodule.map_iSup _ _).symm
86	      rw [h2, hsup, Submodule.map_top, Submodule.range_mkQ]
87	    have h3 : ∀ m, f m ≤ f n₀ := fun m => by
88	      rcases le_total m n₀ with h | h
89	      · exact f.mono h
90	      · exact (hn₀ m h).ge
91	    have h4 : (⊤ : Submodule R (M ⧸ A 0)) ≤ f n₀ := by
92	      rw [← h1]; exact iSup_le h3
93	    exact le_antisymm le_top h4
94	  refine ⟨n₀, fun n hn => ?_⟩
95	  have hfn : (A n).map (A 0).mkQ = ⊤ := by
96	    have h5 : f n = ⊤ := by rw [← hn₀ n hn]; exact hftop
97	    exact h5
98	  have hcomap := congrArg (Submodule.comap (A 0).mkQ) hfn
99	  rwa [Submodule.comap_map_mkQ, Submodule.comap_top,
100	    sup_eq_right.mpr (hmono (Nat.zero_le n))] at hcomap
101	
102	end Stabilization

119	/-- **The fiber lattice inside the fixed ambient overlap module** (the FLV-2(b) bridge

170	      × ((Y.divisorSheaf K D').obj.obj (op (fiberChart₁ π)))) :

176	  have h1 : divisorVal K

195	private lemma range_moduleDiff_eq_comap (D : Y.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ) :
196	    LinearMap.range ((Y.twoCoverSquare (fiberChart₀ π) (fiberChart₁ π)
197	        (preimage_chartOpen_sup π)).moduleDiff
198	        (Y.divisorSheaf K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π)))
199	      = (fiberLattice π D n).comap
200	          (divisorSections K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π)
201	            (fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π)).subtype := by
202	  refine le_antisymm ?_ ?_
203	  · rintro y ⟨t, rfl⟩
204	    have hmem : divisorVal K ((Y.twoCoverSquare (fiberChart₀ π) (fiberChart₁ π)
205	          (preimage_chartOpen_sup π)).moduleDiff
206	          (Y.divisorSheaf K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π)) t) ∈ fiberLattice π D n := by
207	      rw [divisorVal_moduleDiff π (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π) t]
208	      exact Submodule.sub_mem _ (Submodule.mem_sup_left (divisorVal_mem K t.1))
209	        (Submodule.mem_sup_right (divisorVal_mem K t.2))
210	    exact hmem
211	  · intro y hy
212	    have hy' : divisorVal K y ∈ fiberLattice π D n := hy
213	    obtain ⟨a, ha, b, hb, hab⟩ := Submodule.mem_sup.mp hy'
214	    refine ⟨((⟨a, ha⟩ : divisorSections K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π) (fiberChart₀ π)),
215	      (⟨-b, Submodule.neg_mem _ hb⟩ :
216	        divisorSections K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π) (fiberChart₁ π))), ?_⟩
217	    refine divisorSection_ext K ?_
218	    rw [divisorVal_moduleDiff π (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π)]
219	    have hfin : a - (-b) = divisorVal K y := by
220	      rw [sub_neg_eq_add]
221	      exact hab
222	    exact hfin

224	/-- Mapping the comap of a submodule along `LinearEquiv.ofEq` of equal submodules is the
225	comap along the other subtype. -/

section Scaffolding

variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]

/-- The one-point Weil divisor `n · x` at a closed point `x`, as a `CurveDivisor`. The
wrapper `CurveDivisor` is a plain `def` over `Finsupp`, which blocks elaboration of mixed
`Finsupp`/`CurveDivisor` arithmetic; this smart constructor keeps one-point divisors on
the `CurveDivisor` side of the seam. -/
noncomputable def Scheme.CurveDivisor.single {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (n : ℤ) :
    X.CurveDivisor :=
  Finsupp.single (⟨x, hx⟩ : {p : X // p ≠ genericPoint X}) n

/-- The underlying finitely supported function of a one-point divisor. -/
lemma Scheme.CurveDivisor.toFinsupp_single {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (n : ℤ) :
    toFinsupp (CurveDivisor.single hx n) =
      Finsupp.single (⟨x, hx⟩ : {p : X // p ≠ genericPoint X}) n :=
  rfl

/-- The dévissage twist is subtraction of the one-point divisor: `D − x` literally. -/
lemma devissageDivisor_eq_sub {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (D : X.CurveDivisor) :
    devissageDivisor hx D = D - CurveDivisor.single hx 1 :=
  rfl

/-- The one-point divisor with multiplicity `0` is the zero divisor. -/
lemma Scheme.CurveDivisor.single_zero {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) :
    CurveDivisor.single hx 0 = (0 : X.CurveDivisor) := by
  change Finsupp.single (⟨x, hx⟩ : {p : X // p ≠ genericPoint X}) (0 : ℤ) = 0
  exact Finsupp.single_zero _

/-- One-point divisors at the same point add their multiplicities. -/
lemma Scheme.CurveDivisor.single_add {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (m n : ℤ) :
    CurveDivisor.single hx m + CurveDivisor.single hx n = CurveDivisor.single hx (m + n) := by
  change Finsupp.single (⟨x, hx⟩ : {p : X // p ≠ genericPoint X}) m +
      Finsupp.single ⟨x, hx⟩ n = Finsupp.single ⟨x, hx⟩ (m + n)
  exact (Finsupp.single_add _ _ _).symm

section Devissage

variable (K : Type u) [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]

private theorem moduleFinite_hModule_divisorSheaf_aux (D : X.CurveDivisor) :
    Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K D) 0) ∧
      Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K D) 1) := by
  refine Scheme.CurveDivisor.induction_devissage
    (P := fun D => Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K D) 0) ∧
      Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K D) 1))
    ⟨?_, ?_⟩ (fun {x} hx D => ?_) D
  · exact Module.Finite.equiv (Sheaf.HModule.mapEquiv (moduleKSheafDivisorSheafZeroIso K) 0)
  · exact Module.Finite.equiv (Sheaf.HModule.mapEquiv (moduleKSheafDivisorSheafZeroIso K) 1)
  · -- the dévissage step, both ways, through the six-term slice
    have hS := devissageSES_shortExact K hx D
    -- the skyscraper term of the slice, in the `devissageSES` spelling
    haveI hsky0 : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₃ 0) :=
      haveI := moduleFinite_jumpModule K hx D
      moduleFinite_hModule_skyModule_zero x (jumpModule K hx D)
    haveI hsky1 : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₃ 1) :=
      moduleFinite_hModule_skyModule_one x (jumpModule K hx D)
    haveI hskysub : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₃ 1) :=
      skyModule_subsingleton_hModule_one x (jumpModule K hx D)
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨h0D, h1D⟩
      haveI hX₂0 : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₂ 0) := h0D
      haveI hX₂1 : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₂ 1) := h1D
      exact ⟨Sheaf.HModule.moduleFinite_left_zero hS,
        Sheaf.HModule.moduleFinite_left_succ hS (show 0 + 1 = 1 from rfl)⟩
    · rintro ⟨h0D', h1D'⟩
      haveI hX₁0 : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₁ 0) := h0D'
      haveI hX₁1 : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₁ 1) := h1D'
      exact ⟨Sheaf.HModule.moduleFinite_middle hS 0, Sheaf.HModule.moduleFinite_middle hS 1⟩

dévissage from the structure sheaf (whose `H⁰`/`H¹` finiteness are the two instance
hypotheses — properness enters only through them). -/
instance moduleFinite_hModule_divisorSheaf_zero (D : X.CurveDivisor) :
    Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K D) 0) :=
  (moduleFinite_hModule_divisorSheaf_aux K D).1

instance moduleFinite_hModule_divisorSheaf_one (D : X.CurveDivisor) :
    Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K D) 1) :=

import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Chi

/-!
# `h⁰` and `h¹` of a Čech Picard class are well-defined

For the curve bundle `X` — integral, smooth of relative dimension one and quasi-compact over a
field `K` — the sheaf cohomology of a divisor sheaf depends only on the Čech Picard *class* of
the divisor, **separately in each degree**. If two Weil divisors `D`, `D'` have equal class
(`CurveDivisor.picClass K D = CurveDivisor.picClass K D'`) then `D − D' = div g` for a rational
function `g` (extraction `(X)`, `CurveDivisor.exists_divOf_of_picClass_eq`), and multiplication
by `g` is an isomorphism of divisor sheaves `𝒪(D) ≅ 𝒪(D − div g) = 𝒪(D')`
(`Scheme.mulEquivDivisorSheaf`). Transporting the ledger invariants of `RiemannRoch/Chi.lean`
along this isomorphism gives the degreewise statements below.

This is the **W6-lite** brick of the Wave-4 FLV worksheet (`informal/w4-flv-worksheet.md` §3.1):
it collapses to a few lines on the landed `h0_congr`/`h1_congr`/`mapEquiv` API and the landed
multiplication isomorphism, and it closes the FLV-facing form of the degree-lane AMENDMENT debt
(`informal/deg-d2-meromorphic-worksheet.md` §"AMENDMENT 2026-07-15"). Every declaration is the
carbon copy, in a fixed cohomological degree, of the landed Euler-characteristic twin
`AlgebraicGeometry.chi_divisorSheaf_eq_of_picClass_eq` (`RiemannRoch/Degree.lean`), and it
carries the same (finiteness-free) hypothesis budget as that twin.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.h0_divisorSheaf_eq_of_picClass_eq`: `𝒪(D) = 𝒪(D') → h⁰(𝒪(D)) = h⁰(𝒪(D'))`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.h1_divisorSheaf_eq_of_picClass_eq`: `𝒪(D) = 𝒪(D') → h¹(𝒪(D)) = h¹(𝒪(D'))`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_hModule_one_of_picClass_eq`: the vanishing of `H¹` transports
  from `D` to any `D'` of the same class — the `Subsingleton` form the FLV consumers need (it is
  what `HModule.mapEquiv` transports, and it is strictly stronger than `h¹ = 0`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.moduleFinite_hModule_divisorSheaf_zero_of_picClass_eq` /
  `..._one_of_picClass_eq`: finite-dimensionality of `H⁰`/`H¹` transports between divisors of
  equal class (`Module.Finite.equiv` along the same isomorphism).

## Packaging decision (recorded per the W6-lite charter)

The FLV consumers (`informal/w4-flv-worksheet.md` §2.5 step 4, and the §1.2 rank corollary) use
witness-independence *directly* as the equalities/transports above, always on `h⁰`/`h¹` of a
concrete witness `divisorSheaf K D`. They never need a choice-based `h0OfClass`/`h1OfClass`
package. Introducing such packaged definitions would add a `Classical.choice`-of-witness
indirection with no current consumer, so — mirroring the deliberate scope of §3.1, which lists
exactly the `h¹`-eq lemma, the `Subsingleton` transport and the `h⁰` twin — the packaged
"cohomology of a class" definitions are **not** introduced here; the eq-lemmas and transports are
the honest, choice-free interface FLV consumes. (The analogous `classDeg` package in
`Degree.lean` earns its keep only because it is itself the E-i..E-iii interface object; there is
no such downstream demand for an `h⁰`/`h¹` package.)
-/

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

open Scheme

variable (K : Type u) [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
  [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]

/-- **The multiplication isomorphism identifying divisor sheaves of equal class.** For Weil
divisors `D`, `D'` with `CurveDivisor.picClass K D = CurveDivisor.picClass K D'`, the extraction
lemma writes `D − D' = div g`, and multiplication by `g` realizes an isomorphism of sheaves of
`K`-modules `𝒪(D) ≅ 𝒪(D')`. This is the single geometric input shared by every degreewise
statement below (compare the identically-built `hiso` inside
`chi_divisorSheaf_eq_of_picClass_eq`). -/
private noncomputable def picClassDivisorSheafIso {D D' : X.CurveDivisor}
    (h : CurveDivisor.picClass K D = CurveDivisor.picClass K D') :
    X.divisorSheaf K D ≅ X.divisorSheaf K D' := by
  have hg := (CurveDivisor.exists_divOf_of_picClass_eq K h).choose_spec
  have hiso := mulEquivDivisorSheaf K (CurveDivisor.exists_divOf_of_picClass_eq K h).choose D
  rw [show D - Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
    (CurveDivisor.exists_divOf_of_picClass_eq K h).choose = D' by rw [← hg]; abel] at hiso
  exact hiso

/-! ## `h⁰` and `h¹` of a class are well-defined -/

/-- **`h⁰` is a Čech Picard class invariant**: Weil divisors of equal class have the same
`h⁰(𝒪(D))`. Carbon copy of `chi_divisorSheaf_eq_of_picClass_eq` with `Sheaf.h0_congr` in place of
`Sheaf.chi_congr`; needs no finiteness hypotheses. -/
theorem h0_divisorSheaf_eq_of_picClass_eq {D D' : X.CurveDivisor}
    (h : CurveDivisor.picClass K D = CurveDivisor.picClass K D') :
    Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K D) = Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K D') :=
  Sheaf.h0_congr (picClassDivisorSheafIso K h)

/-- **`h¹` is a Čech Picard class invariant**: Weil divisors of equal class have the same
`h¹(𝒪(D))`. Carbon copy of `chi_divisorSheaf_eq_of_picClass_eq` with `Sheaf.h1_congr` in place of
`Sheaf.chi_congr`; needs no finiteness hypotheses. This is the witness-independence that makes the
FLV outer quantifier `∀ D, picClass D = λθⁿ → …` well-posed. -/
theorem h1_divisorSheaf_eq_of_picClass_eq {D D' : X.CurveDivisor}
    (h : CurveDivisor.picClass K D = CurveDivisor.picClass K D') :
    Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K D) = Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K D') :=
  Sheaf.h1_congr (picClassDivisorSheafIso K h)

/-! ## The `Subsingleton` transport (the strong FLV form) -/

/-- **Vanishing of `H¹` is a class invariant**: if the degree-one cohomology of `𝒪(D)` is a
subsingleton (the strong vanishing form), so is that of `𝒪(D')` for any `D'` of the same class.
This is the form the FLV consumers transport (`Subsingleton`, not `h¹ = 0`, since it survives
sheaf isomorphisms and surjections and does not require finite-dimensionality): the isomorphism
`𝒪(D) ≅ 𝒪(D')` induces the `K`-linear equivalence `H¹(𝒪(D)) ≃ₗ[K] H¹(𝒪(D'))`
(`HModule.mapEquiv`), and `Subsingleton` transports across an equivalence. -/
theorem subsingleton_hModule_one_of_picClass_eq {D D' : X.CurveDivisor}
    (h : CurveDivisor.picClass K D = CurveDivisor.picClass K D')
    (hsub : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K D) 1)) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K D') 1) :=
  (Sheaf.HModule.mapEquiv (picClassDivisorSheafIso K h) 1).toEquiv.subsingleton_congr.mp hsub

/-! ## Finite-dimensionality transports -/

/-- **Finiteness of `H⁰` is a class invariant**: if `H⁰(𝒪(D))` is a finite-dimensional
`K`-module, so is `H⁰(𝒪(D'))` for any `D'` of the same class, transported along the class
isomorphism by `Module.Finite.equiv`. -/
theorem moduleFinite_hModule_divisorSheaf_zero_of_picClass_eq {D D' : X.CurveDivisor}
    [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K D) 0)]
    (h : CurveDivisor.picClass K D = CurveDivisor.picClass K D') :
    Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K D') 0) :=
  Module.Finite.equiv (Sheaf.HModule.mapEquiv (picClassDivisorSheafIso K h) 0)

/-- **Finiteness of `H¹` is a class invariant**: if `H¹(𝒪(D))` is a finite-dimensional
`K`-module, so is `H¹(𝒪(D'))` for any `D'` of the same class, transported along the class
isomorphism by `Module.Finite.equiv`. -/
theorem moduleFinite_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_picClass_eq {D D' : X.CurveDivisor}
    [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K D) 1)]
    (h : CurveDivisor.picClass K D = CurveDivisor.picClass K D') :
    Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K D') 1) :=
  Module.Finite.equiv (Sheaf.HModule.mapEquiv (picClassDivisorSheafIso K h) 1)

end AlgebraicGeometry

/-!
# DD-F — the two engines of the bpf-span lemma (descent and tower)

The two window-generic submodule engines of the F3-core proof
(`informal/dd-f-probe-verdict.md` §3c–3e, in the sum-intersection formalization route):

* **the descent engine** `Scheme.descent_baseDivisor_le` (probe 3c): if a submodule `W`
  contains `H⁰(𝒪(C − (A + div h)))` for every nonzero `h` in a subspace `N_L ⊆ H⁰(𝒪(A))`,
  then it contains `H⁰(𝒪(C − bd(N_L)))` — starting from any one `A + div h₁` and
  intersecting with achievers `A + div h_x` one point at a time, each step a
  sum-intersection at levels of depth `≤ 2·deg A`;
* **the tower engine** `Scheme.multiplier_tower_le` (probe 3e, de-Artinianized): for an
  exact-order element `fx` at `x` (`(N₀ + div fx)ₓ = 0`, `N₀ + div fx ≥ 0`),

  `H⁰(𝒪(N₀ + A − E + n·x)) ⊆ H⁰(𝒪(N₀ + A − E)) + fx · H⁰(𝒪(A))`  for `n ≤ Eₓ`,

  climbing the multiplicity of `x` one step at a time: each step is a sum-intersection
  whose second summand is the `fx`-shift of an `A`-window level (this is where the FULL
  multiplier space is spent — the jump of the `A`-side matches the jump of the target,
  which a pencil's 2-dimensional image cannot do once `deg A ≥ 2`; worksheet §3.6(a)).

Both engines take their windows as hypotheses on the divisor levels they visit; the
ledger arithmetic that discharges them lives in the keystone file `BpfSpan.lean`. No `π`,
no ledger constants appear here.
-/

import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.SectionSpaces

/-!
# DD-F brick 1 — the base divisor of a subspace of `H⁰(𝒪(A))`

The normalization vocabulary of the P-fib route (`informal/dat-d-worksheet.md` §3.3 F1,
`informal/dd-f-probe-verdict.md` inventory brick 1): for a subspace `T ⊆ H⁰(𝒪(A))` of the
global sections of a divisor sheaf with a nonzero element, the **base divisor**
`bd(T) = ∑ₓ min_{0 ≠ f ∈ T} (A + div f)ₓ · x` records, at each closed point, the deepest
common zero of the shifted divisors `A + div f ≥ 0`. Provided:

* `Scheme.baseDivisorAt` — the pointwise minimum, as a `ℕ`-valued `sInf` (well-defined
  since `T ⊆ H⁰(𝒪(A))` makes every `A + div f` effective);
* `Scheme.baseDivisor` — the assembled Weil divisor, finitely supported because it is
  bounded by any one `A + div f₀`;
* `baseDivisor_nonneg`, `coeffAt_baseDivisor` — effectivity and the pointwise value;
* `baseDivisorAt_le_coeffAt` — the lower-bound property (`bd(T) ≤ A + div f` for every
  nonzero `f ∈ T`);
* `exists_coeffAt_eq_baseDivisorAt` — the **achiever**: at every closed point some
  nonzero `f ∈ T` attains the minimum (`Nat.sInf_mem`);
* `le_divisorSections_sub_baseDivisor` — `T ⊆ H⁰(𝒪(A − bd T))`;
* `exists_achiever_baseDivisor_sub` — **no residual base point**: relative to
  `A − bd T`, the subspace `T` has an exact-order element at every closed point. This is
  the `hbpf` input of the bpf-span lemma (F3-core).

Everything is `ord`/`coeffAt` calculus on `mem_divisorSections_top_iff`; no cohomology.
-/
